requiredFindings.title: The sender's Cancel echo is bound to the plan, not to the correlation actually sent, and the comparison is type-lax
evidence: CANCEL-NULLABILITY (owner delivery2 CancelV1): 'Cancel.executionId is null iff OpenUniverse has not been sent, otherwise its exact value; analysisOrdinal ... otherwise Analyze.analysisOrdinal'. HOST-SEND-SCHEDULE binds slots only by sequence, frameType, chunk coordinates, seal counts and payload byte length, not by payload content.

Probe S (scratch/probe_05.out.json): OpenUniverse sent with executionId 'exec-2026-09-13-0000' (same length as the planned '...0001'), then a Cancel echoing the PLANNED executionId: accepted. That Cancel's executionId is not the value that was sent.
The same transcript with a Cancel echoing the value actually sent: refused SENDER_DIVERGENCE:cancel-echo.
A SnapshotManifest with manifestSha256 substituted by a same-length digest is consumed as complete.
A Cancel with analysisOrdinal False where the planned value is 0 is accepted by consume (Python False == 0). The carrier refuses it (TYPE_UINT64), so the reference sender's 'exact echo' is not exact.
requiredFindings.fix: Bind each slot to its planned payload identity, for example the deterministic-CBOR SHA-256 of the planned envelope payload, or at minimum to the correlation fields (OpenUniverse executionId, Analyze analysisOrdinal). Then derive the expected Cancel from the frames actually consumed, or refuse any divergence from the planned payload. Compare the Cancel by deterministic-CBOR bytes, not by Python equality. Add vectors: a same-length OpenUniverse executionId substitution refused at that slot, and a bool/int ordinal echo refused.

advisories.text: Fact-plane _is_path assessment. This is not a live fact2 contradiction, but the author's framing needs correction and there is a recorded relation-registry duty. (a) fact-plane.v1 normative sharedTypes.CanonicalPath is 'non-empty NFC project-relative path, slash separators, no empty/dot/dot-dot segment, no leading slash or backslash'; the no-C0/C1 clause belongs to CanonicalText. check-fact-plane.py _is_path reuses _is_nfc_text and is therefore stricter than its own normative type. It is the historical deterministic-CBOR v1 profile checker. (b) Retained fact2 admission (identity-model.v3 registered_payload) validates the relation-payload v2 schema and scans only NFC and negative integers. It never calls _is_path, so a legitimate a<LF>b file (admitted by the wire canonical-path-segments law) is not refused by fact2 payload validation. The contract statement 'would still be refused at fact-plane admission' conflates the v1 checker with fact2 admission and should be corrected. (c) The real remaining gap: relation v2 CanonicalPath admits a//b.rs, a/ and a<BEL>b.rs under both pinned and scoped evaluation (scratch/probe_05b.out.json), although the inherited type forbids empty segments and v2 claims every inherited logical restriction survives. FilePayloadV1.path is protected only by its snapshot-inventory join, which was not executed here (no admit_frame run). VcsChangePayloadV1.previousPath and PackagePayloadV1.manifestPath need their join laws checked. Record this explicitly as a relation-registry/fact-plane unit duty; it does not block this unit.

Worker read authority for partially stale fallback sets. The manifest carries stale and failed rows but no usable-row designation. Specify the duty concretely: either the worker recomputes PO-1 (inputBinding ownerFileManifestSha256, dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest, cfgSetId against its own admitted context) and ignores status=failed, or the host sends the owner partition. Name which, with the inputs, before the M3 worker implements it.

Counting carried rows is intentionally stricter than owner usability: a defaulted set of 257 rows with one stale row loses all 256 usable rows. This is accepted as the wire consequence of set identity; keep the vector that pins it.
